event.title: LOCO 4 CoCo
event.subtitle: Five minutes to your next data product

coco._comment: Each message spawns `cortex exec`. Deliberately UNCAPPED - no max-turns, no effort floor, history left on. Cost is managed by observation (see cost_log) not by throttling the visitor.

delivery._comment: Verified constraints: the Gmail MCP exposes create_draft only - no send tool, no attachment parameter - AND its tools do not load under `cortex exec` even with --bypass, though they work in an interactive CoCo session. snowflake.com also publishes DMARC p=reject, so third-party senders are rejected outright. So the game writes a fully-composed email to outbox/ and the operator's interactive session drains it via the loco4coco-ops skill. Swap transport to gmail_api once an OAuth client is proven against Workspace policy.

intake._comment: CoCo gets up and asks who the present is for. Typing is limited to these three fields plus any 'Other' answers.
intake.industry_question: And what world do you work in? I'll fill the library with the right shelves.
intake.confirm_industry: I'm guessing {industry} from {company} - have I got that right?

wake.head: Sending a CoCo POC to my friend

wake.line: CoCo stirs in his igloo, he dreams of sending his friend a *CoCo POC* (proof of concept) present - *that friend is you!*

library.name: The Library
library.heading: Which of these do you actually have?
library.hint: Tick everything that applies. Add your own if it's missing.
library.narrative: This is your library, {first_name}. Every shelf here is data {company} already holds.
library.prompt: The visitor works in {industry} at {company}. In THE LIBRARY they said they already hold: {selection}. Reply in at most 2 short sentences: reflect back the most valuable thing in that list, and name the one Snowflake capability that would unlock it. Warm, plain English, no jargon, no bullet points, no headings, no em dashes.

marketplace.name: The Marketplace
marketplace.heading: What shall we join to it?
marketplace.hint: Real listings from the Snowflake Marketplace, filtered to what you can actually attach in this region. No copying, no pipelines.
marketplace._discovery_comment: manual = the curated, verified marketplace-index.md. Swap to 'agentic' when the Agentic Marketplace Discovery PrPr lands; the panel contract does not change.
marketplace.narrative: These are live datasets you can query the moment you attach them. Nothing to copy, nothing to maintain.
marketplace.prompt: The visitor works in {industry} at {company} and holds: {held}. In THE MARKETPLACE they chose to join these real Snowflake Marketplace listings: {selection}. Reply in at most 2 short sentences: say what joining those lets them answer that they cannot answer today. Refer to the datasets only by the names given above; do not invent any other listing or provider name. Plain English, no bullet points, no em dashes.

workshop.name: The Workshop
workshop.heading: What should it actually do?
workshop.hint: One sentence. What should the finished thing do?
workshop.placeholder: e.g. answer questions about our policies with citations
workshop.narrative: Bench cleared, forge lit. Tell me what the finished thing does and I'll draw up the plan.
workshop.prompt:
The visitor is {first_name}, {industry}, at {company}. They hold: {held}. They will join: {joined}. In THE WORKSHOP they said the POC should: "{input}".

First choose the archetype that matches what they are ACTUALLY trying to do. Pick exactly one of these keys:
talk-to-my-data (ask questions of structured data in plain English)
ask-my-documents (search or Q&A over documents and free text)
extract-from-paperwork (pull structured fields out of forms, invoices, letters)
triage-and-classify (sort, route or prioritise incoming items)
an-agent-that-acts (takes an action, not just answers)
dashboard-that-explains-itself (a visual that narrates the why)
predict-what-happens-next (forecasting or risk scoring)
join-the-silos (unify data that lives in separate systems)
share-without-copying (give someone else live access)
watch-it-live (streaming or near real-time monitoring)

The data they hold decides this. If their source is documents or free text, it is ask-my-documents or extract-from-paperwork, NOT talk-to-my-data.

For features, you MUST choose 2 to 4 names EXACTLY as spelled from this list and nothing else:
{feature_list}

Return ONLY minified JSON, no prose and no code fence, with exactly these keys:
{"archetype": one key from the list above, "poc_name": short name in their own language, max 8 words, "summary": 2 sentences on what it does and why it matters, "features": array of 2-4 names copied exactly from the feature list, "first_step": one concrete first action, "considerations": array of 3 or 4 short specific things they should think about or improve - gaps in their data, unknowns, governance or effort - each one sentence, concrete to THEIR situation and never generic, "readiness": integer 1-5, "reply": max 40 words, warm, spoken aloud to them, no bullet points, no em dashes}

Score readiness strictly and privately: award points only for data they actually named. Do NOT award a 5 unless they named specific data, a specific question, and a specific user. The visitor never sees this number, so be honest rather than kind. Never claim the POC is built.

postbox.heading: Shall I post it?
postbox.hint: I'll write it up properly and put it in the post.
postbox.narrative: Wrapped, labelled and ready. Say the word and it's in the post to {email}.

intro.title: Loco for CoCo
body: This is a fun way to experience the power of Cortex Code (CoCo) through the medium of an arcade game.

You have 5 minutes to explore the key aspects of building out a Proof of Concept on Snowflake with CoCo as your tour guide on our features, marketplace datasets and how enterprise-grade AI can bring your ideas to life.

After 5 minutes you will have a personalised action plan (sent to you via email) to building out a project on Snowflake - be daring! This is a fun, flexible process with a very real and useful outcome!
